skill.name: research-merge
skill.description: Processes Claude Code Web research branches by previewing content, asking for merge decisions, squash-merging approved work, organizing research documents, and creating GitHub issues from findings.
skill.summary: Organizes approved research branches into merged documentation and GitHub issues.
skill.author: jrc1883

security_audit.summary: The high certificate/key alerts are false positives because the script only handles path strings for research comparison. The confirmed risks are the documented git and GitHub CLI operations that can merge commits, move files, create issues, and delete remote research branches after user approval. No evidence found for prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or hidden network behavior.

remediation.issue: Repository and GitHub state changes are executed through CLI commands.
remediation.suggestion: Show the exact git and gh commands before execution, require explicit approval, and stop when the working tree is dirty.

remediation.issue: Remote branch deletion is part of the workflow.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict deletion to refs matching claude/research-* and require a separate confirmation after a successful merge.

remediation.issue: Branch names, issue titles, and issue bodies may come from research content.
remediation.suggestion: Validate branch names and pass generated titles or bodies as structured command arguments instead of interpolated shell text.

content.value_statement: Research created in Claude Code web sessions can stay scattered across branches. This skill guides review, merging, document organization, and issue creation.
actual_capabilities: Detects Claude research branches through a research branch detector utility.
Previews branch topics, document paths, commit counts, and summaries before action.
Prompts the user to merge, merge with an issue, skip, or delete each branch.
Documents git commands for squash merging approved research into the main branch.
Moves research documents into docs/research when they are not already organized.
Creates GitHub issues from research summaries, tasks, labels, and source metadata.
limitations: It is designed only for research branches, not regular feature branches.
It requires git access and the GitHub CLI for the full workflow.
It does not resolve merge conflicts automatically.
Issue quality depends on research documents following the expected format.

use_cases.title: Process mobile research sessions
use_cases.description: Merge research created in Claude Code Web into the main repository with organized documentation.

use_cases.title: Turn findings into tracked work
use_cases.description: Convert research summaries and implementation tasks into GitHub issues with useful labels.

use_cases.title: Maintain research documentation
use_cases.description: Move research documents into a standard docs/research location after approval.

prompt_templates.title: Review research branches
prompt_templates.prompt: Find Claude research branches, preview each branch, and ask before taking any merge, issue, or delete action.

prompt_templates.title: Merge approved research
prompt_templates.prompt: Process the approved research branch, move its documents to docs/research, and summarize the completed actions.

prompt_templates.title: Create implementation issues
prompt_templates.prompt: Merge approved research and create GitHub issues from the summary, source details, and implementation tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Batch process a research queue
prompt_templates.prompt: Review all claude/research branches, group related topics, propose a processing order, and execute only approved actions.

output_examples.input: One approved research branch about audio feedback hooks.
output_examples.output: A completion summary lists the merged branch, organized research document, and created GitHub issue.

output_examples.input: Several research branches with mixed priorities.
output_examples.output: A branch table shows each topic, commit count, document list, selected action, and next step.

output_examples.input: A research document with implementation tasks.
output_examples.output: A GitHub issue draft contains the summary, source branch, documentation links, and task checklist.

best_practices: Review branch previews before approving merge or deletion actions.
Keep research documents in the expected format with summaries and implementation tasks.
Confirm the working tree is clean before running merge operations.
anti_patterns: Do not use this workflow for normal feature branches.
Do not delete remote branches before verifying the merge result.
Do not create issues from incomplete or unreviewed research notes.

faq.question: What branches does this skill process?
faq.answer: It is intended for Claude research branches, especially branches matching claude/research-* or containing research documentation.

faq.question: Does it merge automatically?
faq.answer: The skill instructs the agent to ask for user approval before merge, issue creation, skip, or delete actions.

faq.question: Can it create GitHub issues?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create issues from research summaries, source metadata, implementation tasks, and labels when the GitHub CLI is available.

faq.question: Where are research documents placed?
faq.answer: The workflow moves root-level research documents into docs/research when they are not already there.

faq.question: What happens if conflicts occur?
faq.answer: The skill tells the agent to show conflicts and offer manual resolution instead of resolving them automatically.

faq.question: Is this suitable for feature development branches?
faq.answer: No. The skill description explicitly limits use to research branches and research documentation workflows.
